title: Regulatory Amendment and Evolution of Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016

qa_pairs.scenario: A veteran customs broker sits at his desk in Chittagong, organizing his office files as he prepares for the upcoming fiscal year. He wants to ensure his firm remains fully compliant with the latest regulatory framework introduced by the government on June 2, 2016. He pulls out the official gazette to verify the precise name of the new legislation that now governs his professional licensing. What is the official title of the legal instrument established on June 2, 2016, to regulate customs agents?
qa_pairs.question: What is the official title of the legal instrument established on June 2, 2016, to regulate customs agents?
qa_pairs.answer: The official title is the Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016.

qa_pairs.scenario: A legal compliance officer at a major logistics firm is reviewing the recent updates to the customs brokerage requirements that took effect on July 1, 2016. She needs to clarify the source of the regulatory power behind these changes to ensure her company's operations align with the latest SRO. She references Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 to pinpoint the exact governing body responsible. Which regulatory body is empowered under Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 to amend the Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.question: Which regulatory body is empowered under Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 to amend the Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: The National Board of Revenue is the regulatory body empowered to amend these rules.

qa_pairs.scenario: An internal auditor is conducting a deep-dive review of a brokerage firm's licensing history to prepare for an upcoming government inspection. While examining the legal records from June 2017, he encounters the specific amendment S.R.O. 145-AIN/2017 and needs to document the exact legislative justification for its issuance. He cross-references the Third Schedule of the Customs Act, 1969 to find the specific provision cited in the amendment. Under which specific item of the Third Schedule of the Customs Act, 1969 was the amendment S.R.O. 145-AIN/2017 issued?
qa_pairs.question: Under which specific item of the Third Schedule of the Customs Act, 1969 was the amendment S.R.O. 145-AIN/2017 issued?
qa_pairs.answer: The amendment was issued under Item 21 of the Third Schedule.

qa_pairs.question: What regulatory framework did the Customs Agent Licensing Rules 2016 replace?

qa_pairs.scenario: A senior customs official is reviewing the documentation for a 2017 amendment to the licensing rules to ensure that all procedural actions remain within the scope of the original mandate. He carefully examines the statutory references to confirm that the National Board of Revenue acted within its delegated powers. He turns to the Customs Act, 1969 to locate the exact provision that grants this authority. What section of the Customs Act, 1969 provides the legal authority for the National Board of Revenue to amend customs agent licensing rules?
qa_pairs.question: What section of the Customs Act, 1969 provides the legal authority for the National Board of Revenue to amend customs agent licensing rules?
qa_pairs.answer: Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 provides the legal authority.

qa_pairs.question: When were the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 initially enacted?
qa_pairs.explanation: The timeline explicitly states that the initial enactment of the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 occurred on 2016-06-02.

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument served as the first formal amendment to the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
options: The Third Schedule of the Customs Act
qa_pairs.explanation: According to the timeline, SRO 220-Law/2016/47/Customs, dated 2016-07-01, was the first formal amendment to the 2016 rules.

qa_pairs.question: Under which legal authority does the National Board of Revenue amend the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.explanation: The provided context (specifically the 2016 and 2017 SROs) confirms that the NBR exercises its rule-making power under Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969, read with the Third Schedule.

qa_pairs.question: What was the date of the second formal amendment to the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.explanation: The timeline indicates that the second formal amendment, SRO 145-Law/2017/31/Customs, was promulgated on 2017-06-01.

qa_pairs.question: How did the legal framework for customs agents in Bangladesh evolve from 2009 to 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: The regulatory framework transitioned from the 2009 regulations to the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016, which were enacted on June 2, 2016, to establish a new legal basis for licensing.

qa_pairs.question: What is the legal basis for the National Board of Revenue to amend the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: The National Board of Revenue derives its authority to amend these rules from Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969, read in conjunction with the Third Schedule of the same Act.

qa_pairs.question: How has the National Board of Revenue utilized statutory regulatory orders to refine the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: The NBR utilized statutory regulatory orders to implement iterative amendments, specifically issuing SRO 220-Law/2016/47/Customs on July 1, 2016, and SRO 145-Law/2017/31/Customs on June 1, 2017, to refine operational and regulatory requirements.

qa_pairs.question: What role does the Third Schedule of the Customs Act, 1969 play in the amendment of customs agent regulations?
qa_pairs.answer: The Third Schedule serves as the supplementary legal framework that provides the specific itemized authority under which the National Board of Revenue exercises its rule-making powers to amend licensing regulations, such as the 2017 amendment referencing Item 21.

qa_pairs.question: Why were the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 subjected to formal amendments in 2016 and 2017?
qa_pairs.answer: The rules were amended to refine the operational and regulatory requirements for customs agents, ensuring that the legal framework remained updated under the authority granted by the Customs Act, 1969.

qa_pairs.scenario: A customs agent operating under the legal framework established on June 2, 2016, observes that the National Board of Revenue has issued subsequent regulatory orders on July 1, 2016, and June 1, 2017, to modify the original rules.
qa_pairs.question: What is the legal authority that allows the National Board of Revenue to issue these successive amendments to the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016?
qa_pairs.answer: The amendments are issued under the authority of Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969, read with the Third Schedule (specifically Item 21 in the 2017 amendment).

qa_pairs.question: Following the initial enactment of the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 on June 2, 2016, what formal amendment occurred one month later?
qa_pairs.answer: On July 1, 2016, the National Board of Revenue issued SRO 220-Law/2016/47/Customs, which served as the first formal amendment to the 2016 rules.

qa_pairs.question: What regulatory change occurred exactly one year after the SRO 220-Law/2016/47/Customs amendment was issued?
qa_pairs.answer: On June 1, 2017, the National Board of Revenue issued SRO 145-Law/2017/31/Customs, representing the second formal amendment to the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016.
